tools.name: wave_graphql_query
tools.description: Escape hatch for reads the other tools do not shape the way you need: run one GraphQL query (never a mutation) against Wave's public API and get the raw data. tools.name: wave_create_transaction
tools.description: Record a bank/credit-card transaction and categorize it, as if entered in Wave's Transactions page. Expense paid by card: anchor {accountId: card, direction: WITHDRAWAL}, line {accountId: expense category, balance: INCREASE}. Sale deposited to bank: anchor {bank, DEPOSIT}, line {income account, INCREASE}. Split across several lines; they must total the anchor. Keep the returned id: wave_get_transaction / wave_list_transactions read it back. Use dryRun=true to validate without writing. Wave does not document de-duplication by externalId: if a call timed out, check the Wave web app before retrying.

accountId.description: Category account (income, expense, liability...). Never another bank/card account: transfers are not supported by the API

balance.description: INCREASE (default) grows the category: more income for a sale, more expense for a purchase. DECREASE for refunds. DEBIT/CREDIT for accountants

taxes.description: Sales tax amounts on this line

lineItems.description: How the amount is categorized; must add up to the anchor amount

tools.name: wave_list_transactions
tools.description: List and search the business's transactions as Wave's Transactions page shows them: bank and card transactions, expenses, deposits, transfers, bill and invoice payments. Live data. Filter by date range, text in the description, bank/card account (accountId), category accounts (categoryIds) or uncategorizedOnly. Cursor pagination: pass nextCursor back as cursor. For totals (spend per category, month, vendor or account) use wave_summarize_transactions instead of paging through rows. Each row has the amount, direction, bank/card account, category (or categories when split), vendor, sales tax and review status. IDs work with wave_get_transaction, wave_update_transaction and wave_delete_transaction. Uses Wave's web-app API (unofficial), which needs a web session: if it is missing or expired, the user runs node /pkg/node_modules/@saccolabs/wave-mcp/bin/wave-mcp.js login in a terminal on 44e1b3cb51c2.

tools.name: wave_summarize_transactions
tools.description: Totals over every matching transaction, grouped by category, month, vendor, customer or bank/card account: how much was spent on Marketing this year, spend per month, top vendors. Pages through Wave itself and returns only the totals, so use it instead of paging wave_list_transactions to add things up. Same filters as wave_list_transactions. Sums line amounts (which include sales tax): money-out lines (debits) are withdrawals, money-in lines (credits) are deposits; journal entries count by the same debit/credit rule. With categoryIds, only the lines in those categories count, so split transactions are not double counted. tools.name: wave_update_transaction
tools.description: Edit a transaction as in the Wave web app: date, description, notes, reviewed (verified), bank/card account, total amount, category, vendor or customer, or the full set of split lines. Journal entries (journalEntry: true) have no bank side: edit their lines, keeping debits equal to credits. Single-category transactions: use categoryId / vendorId / customerId / amount / salesTax directly. Split transactions: pass lines (every line to keep, with order from wave_get_transaction; omit order to add a line; lines left out are removed). Line amounts include sales tax and must add up to the amount. Reads the transaction first and sends its current sequence, so it never overwrites a newer edit. dryRun=true shows the change without saving. Confirm with the user before changing amounts or accounts. Uses Wave's web-app API (unofficial), which needs a web session: if it is missing or expired, the user runs node /pkg/node_modules/@saccolabs/wave-mcp/bin/wave-mcp.js login in a terminal on 44e1b3cb51c2.

tools.name: wave_run_report
tools.description: Financial reports computed by this server (Wave's API has no report endpoint). Rows are paginated with limit/offset; totals always cover every row. From the imported ledger (wave_import_ledger; any period, default year to date; balance-sheet style reports as of endDate): profit_and_loss, balance_sheet, cash_flow, trial_balance, account_balances, account_transactions/general_ledger (filter with account or accountId), sales_tax (sales and purchases), aged_payables, purchases_by_vendor. Without a ledger, profit_and_loss, balance_sheet, trial_balance and account_balances fall back to current account balances from the API (as of now only), and sales_tax to invoices. Live from invoices (invoice date range): income_by_customer, sales_by_product, invoice_summary; as of today: aged_receivables; customer_statement needs customerId. Not possible: tax_line, payroll_wage_tax, payroll_benefits_deductions.

tools.name: wave_import_ledger
tools.description: Load the full transaction journal from Wave's Data Export so transactions can be listed and date-range reports run. Wave's public API cannot read transactions; this is the supported way to get them. Get the file: Wave → Settings → Data Export → Accounting (CSV) → Export; Wave emails a download link (valid 24 hours). Pass the path of the downloaded .zip (or the accounting .csv inside it) on the machine running this server. Replaces any earlier import for the business. Nothing is sent to Wave; the ledger is stored locally (mode 600).

path.description: Absolute path to the Data Export .zip or its accounting .csv

businessId.description: Business ID; defaults to the one wave_get_context reports

annotations.title: Import transactions from a Wave Data Export

tools.name: wave_list_ledger_transactions
tools.description: List and search transactions from an imported Data Export snapshot (wave_import_ledger). For live data use wave_list_transactions; this works offline and includes invoices, bills and journal entries: bank and card transactions, expenses, invoices, bills, payments, transfers and journal entries. Filter by date range, account (ID or name), text, customer, vendor, amount, direction or uncategorized only. Newest first by default. Each row has the amount on the bank/card account (or the journal total), the categories used, and the transaction ID for wave_get_ledger_transaction.

instructions:
Wave accounting (waveapps.com). Call wave_get_context first; if credentials are missing or expired the user signs in with node /pkg/node_modules/@saccolabs/wave-mcp/bin/wave-mcp.js login in a terminal on 44e1b3cb51c2. Full guide: the wave://guide resource.
- Uses Wave's public GraphQL API, plus Wave's web-app API for transactions.
- Call wave_get_context first: it shows the businesses this credential reaches and the default one. Every other tool takes an optional businessId.
- Lists are paginated (page/pageSize, or offset/limit for reports and payments). Ask for small pages, follow nextPage/nextOffset only when needed, and prefer detail="summary".
- Transactions (live): wave_list_transactions, wave_summarize_transactions, wave_get_transaction, wave_update_transaction and wave_delete_transaction use Wave's web-app API, which needs a browser session (wave_get_context shows auth.webSession). Sessions end when the user signs out of Wave or they time out; then ask the user to run node /pkg/node_modules/@saccolabs/wave-mcp/bin/wave-mcp.js login in a terminal on 44e1b3cb51c2 and paste a request copied from the Wave web app (the command explains how). No restart is needed. For totals (spend per category, month or vendor) call wave_summarize_transactions rather than paging through rows. accountId filters by the bank/card account; categoryIds by income/expense category. Edits send the transaction's sequence, so they never overwrite a newer change.
- Wave's public API has no reports. wave_run_report computes them from an imported Data Export (wave_import_ledger, a snapshot: check ledger.importedAt) or falls back to invoices and current balances; every report states its basis. wave_list_ledger_transactions searches that snapshot.
- Never ask the user to paste access tokens, session tokens or curl commands into the chat. The user sets credentials in a terminal on 44e1b3cb51c2: node /pkg/node_modules/@saccolabs/wave-mcp/bin/wave-mcp.js login (pastes a request copied from the browser) or node /pkg/node_modules/@saccolabs/wave-mcp/bin/wave-mcp.js secrets set WAVE_ACCESS_TOKEN. You may run node /pkg/node_modules/@saccolabs/wave-mcp/bin/wave-mcp.js check yourself to verify; it prints no secrets.
- Writes change real books. wave_send_* tools email real customers; confirm recipients and amounts with the user first. wave_create_transaction supports dryRun.
- Line items on invoices and estimates must reference a product (wave_list_products).
- Not available at all: bills, bill payments, reconciliation, receipts and tags (see wave://limitations). Say so instead of searching for them; aged_payables needs an imported Data Export.
